topic: Transitioning from web development to embedded/firmware engineering
sourceTitle: Ask HN: Tips for transitioning from web development to embedded/firmware?
postText:
Thinking about swapping your JavaScript stack for firmware?

- Identify core concepts that translate: problem solving, version control, testing. Using Git for firmware keeps the workflow familiar. That continuity speeds up onboarding and reduces context-switch friction.

- Fill the hardware knowledge gap: learn C/C++, memory constraints, and real-time OS basics. Cheap dev boards like an Arduino or Raspberry Pi Pico give instant hands-on experience. Start with blinking an LED; it teaches timing and pin control instantly.

- Adjust your debugging mindset: move from console logs to oscilloscopes, JTAG, and hardware breakpoints. Serial output remains a trusty ally for quick checks. Don’t forget to log register states; they reveal hidden bugs faster than any print.

- Re-think performance budgeting: web apps can waste megabytes; embedded forces you to count every byte and cycle. I shaved a firmware image from 256 KB to 64 KB by trimming unused libraries. Every kilobyte you save can lower flash cost and extend battery life.

- Leverage cloud tools for IoT: AWS IoT Core lets your device talk to the same dashboards you built for web users, keeping your front-end chops useful. You can even push OTA updates using the same CI pipelines you already have.

What’s the biggest surprise you’ve faced moving from the browser to the board?
